column1: # Easyport translation rules — Forge 1.20.1 -> NeoForge 1.21.1
# Lines are  kind <TAB> from <TAB> to  (to omitted for REMOVED). Blank lines and # ignored.
# Deliberately small. Under shim-first, most loader-API references need no rewriting at all:
# forge-compat ships a real net.minecraftforge.* tree, so a mod's existing references resolve
# against it untouched. Rules are only needed where a shim is impossible — which in practice
# means net.minecraft.*, since that package is owned by the game and cannot be shadowed.
# SRG -> official member renaming is not expressed here. It is 64,225 entries and lives in
# mappings/srg2official.tsv, applied automatically before any rule below is matched. Rules
# are therefore written against *official* names.
# Rule kinds
#   CTOR_TO_STATIC   a constructor became a static factory. Rewrites NEW/DUP/INVOKESPECIAL
#                    into a single INVOKESTATIC. Real bytecode surgery, not a rename.
#   RENAME_METHOD    same shape, different owner or name. A plain call-site rewrite.
#   REMOVED          no replacement exists. Reported, never silently rewritten -- inventing a
#                    target here is exactly the failure mode measured in handport/ (5 false
#                    positives out of 26 symbols).
# --- Loader-scanned annotations: the hard exception to shim-first -------------------------
# These MUST be rewritten and cannot be shimmed. FML discovers mods by scanning class files
# for the exact annotation descriptor `Lnet/neoforged/fml/common/Mod;`. A shimmed
# net.minecraftforge.fml.common.Mod in forge-compat is a *different type* as far as that scan
# is concerned, so the mod is never found and never constructed -- it loads, registers
# nothing, and reports no error, which is the worst possible failure mode.
# Measured: additional_lights translated cleanly, loaded, and contributed 0 of 326 entries
# purely because its @Mod annotation still said net.minecraftforge.
# The rule of thumb: anything the *loader itself* looks up by name must be rewritten.
# Everything a mod merely calls can be shimmed.
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
# --- Event types: dispatched by identity, so also unshimmable ---------------------------
# The event bus resolves a listener's target from the declared parameter type and dispatches
# by exact class. A shimmed FMLCommonSetupEvent would be a distinct class from the one the bus
# actually posts, so the listener would register successfully and then simply never fire --
# again silent, again the worst kind of failure.
# Same rule as the annotations above: the loader dispatches these, so they must be rewritten.
# A mod only *calls* ForgeConfigSpec, so that one can stay shimmed.

# --- ResourceLocation: constructor privatised in 1.21 -------------------------------------
# The single largest vanilla dependency in the corpus: 237 + 188 mods.

# 135 / 111 / 105 / 97 mods. These are NOT renames: the whole idiom changed, and a call-site
# rewrite cannot express getOrCreateTag() returning a mutable tag backed by the stack.
# Recorded as REMOVED so the transformer reports them instead of guessing. The vanilla bridge
# (Phase 4) is what actually resolves these.
REMOVED

# --- Formerly listed as removed; both are now shimmed ------------------------------------
# FMLJavaModLoadingContext#get and ModLoadingContext#get were recorded here as having no
# replacement, on the reasoning that NeoForge injects the bus into the mod constructor. That
# was wrong: NeoForge kept ModLoadingContext.get() and exposes the bus through
# getActiveContainer().getEventBus(), so both are plain delegating shims in forge-compat.
# Left as a note rather than deleted, because a stale REMOVED entry is actively harmful --
# every translation report flagged a resolved symbol as unresolvable, which sends whoever
# reads the report chasing work that is already done.
# --- Vanilla constructors whose arguments were reordered ---------------------------------
# CTOR_SWAP2  owner <TAB> oldDesc <TAB> newDesc <TAB> [narrowTopTo]
# TorchBlock went from (Properties, ParticleOptions) to (SimpleParticleType, Properties) in
# 1.21 -- reordered and narrowed at once. The narrowing needs a CHECKCAST emitted before the
# swap, while the value is still reachable on top of the stack.
CTOR_SWAP2
CTOR_SWAP2
# RENAME_METHOD  owner <TAB> name <TAB> desc <TAB> newOwner <TAB> newName <TAB> newDesc
# The kind a rename table handles well -- and the kind corpus mining scored 13 out of 13 on in
# the hand-port. Kept explicit rather than auto-imported from candidate-rules-strong.tsv so
# every entry has been checked; the mining is a source of leads, not of truth.
RENAME_METHOD
# TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME  fromPrefix <TAB> toPrefix
# A prefix rename is normally the wrong tool -- a blanket net.minecraftforge -> net.neoforged
# rename would defeat the shim layer entirely. It is correct here precisely because these
# packages contain nothing but event classes, and events are dispatched by exact class
# identity, so every one of them must be rewritten. Enumerating several hundred individually
# would be noise, and any that got missed would fail silently by simply never firing.
# Exact TYPE_RENAME entries above still win: they are checked first.
# TickEvent is bridged in forge-compat rather than renamed: NeoForge split one phase-carrying
# class into Pre/Post, and renaming ClientTickEvent to ClientTickEvent$Post would silently
# misfire every START-phase listener. Exact renames are checked before prefixes, so an explicit
# no-op entry keeps the prefix rule from touching it.
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME
TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME
TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME
# Supersedes the nine individual FML lifecycle TYPE_RENAME entries above: net/neoforged/fml/
# event/ covers both the lifecycle and config trees, so one rule replaces them and there are
# eight fewer places for the list to drift out of date. Also picks up ModConfigEvent, which
# the hand-written list had simply missed.
TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME
# --- Removed vanilla types: relocate, then rename -----------------------------------------
# 1.21 deleted these outright. Supplying the class in its original package is impossible --
# net.minecraft is owned by the game's module and a second jar exporting into it fails module
# resolution (proven in testkit/vanilla-package-probe). So forge-compat carries a stand-in
# under easyport.vanilla and references are rewritten to it.
# Restores loading, not behaviour: vanilla drives loot serialization through codecs now and
# will never call the shim's methods, so custom loot conditions and functions stay inert. The
# rest of the mod works. Generating a codec from the mod's serialize/deserialize pair is
# Phase 4 vanilla-bridge work.
TYPE_RENAME
# Same shape as TorchBlock: 1.21 moved the Properties argument last. No narrowing needed here,
# both arguments are already the right types.
CTOR_SWAP2
# Shim-first exists because most Forge APIs do not map cleanly onto NeoForge. These do: same
# class, same name, different namespace. Renaming is cheaper than writing and maintaining a
# shim that would only forward every call verbatim.
# The risk is that a signature differs somewhere inside one of them, which shows up as
# NoSuchMethodError rather than ClassNotFoundException. If that happens, convert that specific
# entry to a shim -- a shim can adapt a signature where a rename cannot.
# These block the eight highest-fan-in library mods in the corpus, which together have ~70
# dependents. Fixing a library is worth many tail mods.
TYPE_RENAME
# ModLoader removed from this list: renaming resolved the class and then failed on
# isDataGenRunning(), which NeoForge does not have. It is a shim in forge-compat instead.
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
# RegisterEvent is dispatched by identity like every other event, so it must be renamed
# regardless of whether a shim would have been possible.
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
# NewRegistryEvent survived the fork under the same name in NeoForge's package, and NeoForge
# still posts it on the mod bus -- so unlike TickEvent this needs no bridge, only a rename.
# 22 corpus jars reference it, including architectury and cyclopscore.
# Known sharp edge: the two versions agree on the class but not on all of its methods. Forge's
# create(RegistryBuilder) returned Supplier<IForgeRegistry<V>>; NeoForge's returns Registry<T>
# and takes its own RegistryBuilder. Mods that only *receive* the event -- cyclopscore ignores
# its argument entirely -- are fine. Mods that call create() will surface a NoSuchMethodError,
# which is loud, and the fix at that point is to convert this entry to a shim that adapts the
# signature. Renaming first because it costs one line and covers the common case.
TYPE_RENAME
# ModContainer moved package but kept its shape. cyclopscore names it in six classes.
TYPE_RENAME
# TextureStitchEvent.Post became TextureAtlasStitchedEvent -- a rename the scoped prefix rule for
# net/minecraftforge/client/event/ cannot express, since the simple name changed too. The prefix
# rule produced neoforge/client/event/TextureStitchEvent$Post, which does not exist, and the
# target-existence check correctly refused it -- leaving the original name to fail at load.
# Pre has no counterpart: NeoForge removed pre-stitch sprite injection entirely. Left unmapped
# deliberately, so a mod that uses it fails loudly rather than binding to the wrong event.
# 16 corpus jars reference this family; architectury's listener is an empty method.
TYPE_RENAME
# Biome modification survived the fork nearly intact -- same names, NeoForge's package.
# 37 corpus jars.
# One known incompatibility, deliberately accepted: Forge's BiomeModifier.codec() returns
# Codec<? extends BiomeModifier>, NeoForge's returns MapCodec. A renamed implementation still
# declares the Codec-returning method, so it no longer overrides anything and calling codec()
# through the interface throws AbstractMethodError. That is loud and late rather than silent,
# and the mod loads -- where without the rename it does not load at all.
# The underlying cause is the 1.20.5 Codec/MapCodec split, which affects far more than biomes
# and needs its own pass. Recorded in ROADMAP rather than worked around here.
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
# Wholesale package moves.
# Derived from api-report/unresolved-types.txt, which lists every Forge type the corpus actually
# references that nothing currently resolves, alongside any platform class with the same name.
# NeoForge reorganised namespaces far more than it renamed things, so most of the list is one
# package move repeated -- these rules are that observation written down.
# Broad prefixes are safe here specifically because Translate refuses a rename whose target does
# not exist in the platform index (see renameTargetExists). A prefix that overreaches produces a
# missing target and is dropped, leaving the original name to be resolved by a shim or to fail
# loudly. That property is what makes it reasonable to map a whole package rather than enumerate
# it -- and it is why these must never be added without the platform jars indexed.
# Counts are jars in the 433-jar ATM9 corpus referencing the busiest type in each package.
TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME
TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME
TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME
TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME

TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME

TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME
TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME
# Tags is a single class whose nested tag holders (Tags$Items, Tags$Blocks) are what mods use.
# Written as a prefix so the nested types come along without enumerating them.
TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME
# Renamed packages, where the target path is not a mechanical substitution of the source.
TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME
TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME
TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME
# Capabilities: deliberately NOT renamed. This rule existed briefly and was wrong.
# The names survived the move, so a prefix rule looks like it works -- ICapabilityProvider and
# RegisterCapabilitiesEvent both exist under net/neoforged/neoforge/capabilities/. The shapes did
# not survive:
#   Forge     ICapabilityProvider          { LazyOptional<T> getCapability(Capability<T>, Direction) }
#   NeoForge  ICapabilityProvider<O, C, T> { T getCapability(O, C) }
# 106 corpus jars *implement* Forge's interface. Renaming makes each of them declare a method
# that overrides nothing and leaves NeoForge's abstract method unimplemented -- the class still
# loads, and fails with AbstractMethodError whenever something asks it for a capability, which
# may be deep into a game. RegisterCapabilitiesEvent is the same story: it exists, and its
# register(Class) -- called by 68 jars -- does not.
# Both were caught by the member check in tools/RenameGaps.java rather than by a launch, which
# is the point of that check. Left unresolved and visible in the gap report until the capability
# bridge is designed; a rename that resolves onto an incompatible type is worse than no rule,
# because the gap report then stops mentioning it.
# --- Restructured events: renamed, not merely moved -------------------------------------------
# READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE BLOCK BELOW.
# These renames are load-enabling stopgaps, not correct translations. NeoForge renamed the
# events' *accessors* along with the events, and a type rename cannot follow that:
#   LivingHurtEvent.getAmount()        -> LivingDamageEvent$Pre has getNewDamage()
#   EntityItemPickupEvent.getEntity()  -> ItemEntityPickupEvent$Pre has getPlayer()
#   SpawnPlacementRegisterEvent.register(...) -> different signature entirely
# So a renamed listener resolves its event, registers, fires -- and throws NoSuchMethodError on
# the first accessor it touches. Every instance is listed by the member check in RenameGaps.
# Kept anyway, deliberately: without them the mod does not load at all and contributes nothing,
# whereas with them it loads, registers its content, and fails only if that specific event
# actually fires. Loud and narrow beats total and silent. But they are a stepping stone.
# The real fix is the shim-and-bridge shape already used for TickEvent: a forge-compat class
# carrying the Forge accessor names, plus a bridge subscribing to the NeoForge event and
# re-posting the Forge-shaped one. That is the plan for the whole restructured-event family and
# it is not done.
# The prefix rules above handle events NeoForge only repackaged. These are the ones it also
# renamed or split, where a prefix rule either produces a missing target (harmless -- refused and
# reported) or, far worse, lands on a real class that is never posted.
# Damage events were reordered and renamed together. NeoForge's own migration guidance gives the
# mapping, which is not guessable from the names:
#   LivingAttackEvent  fires before any reduction        -> LivingIncomingDamageEvent
#   LivingHurtEvent    fires after reduction, before use -> LivingDamageEvent$Pre
#   LivingDamageEvent  fires after damage is applied     -> LivingDamageEvent$Post
# The third is the dangerous one and the reason tools/RenameGaps.java now flags abstract targets.
# Forge's LivingDamageEvent is concrete and posted; NeoForge kept the name as an *abstract* parent
# for its Pre/Post pair. The prefix rule resolved it happily, and 24 jars' listeners would have
# registered against a class nothing ever posts -- loading cleanly and silently doing nothing.
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
# Ticking moved out of the per-entity event and into the shared tick package. Forge's
# LivingTickEvent had no phase field -- it fired once, cancellably, before the tick -- so Pre is
# an exact match rather than the coin-flip that Pre/Post mapping usually is.
# Withdrawn: LivingTickEvent -> EntityTickEvent$Pre.
# The event does correspond, but Forge's getEntity() returns LivingEntity and NeoForge's returns
# Entity, so all 41 jars calling it would take a NoSuchMethodError -- a rename cannot narrow a
# return type. Needs a shim that wraps the NeoForge event and re-declares the accessor, which is
# the same bridging shape as TickEvent. Flagged by the member check, not by a launch.
# TYPE_RENAME
# Pickup split into a cancellable Pre and an informational Post. Forge had one of each already
# under different names, so both map cleanly.
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
# Straight renames.

TYPE_RENAME
# ForgeEventFactory was split in two. Neither half is a superset, so this needs per-method rules
# rather than a type rename; left unmapped until the methods are mined. 80 jars, so it matters.
#   net/neoforged/neoforge/event/EventHooks     -- posting game events
#   net/neoforged/neoforge/common/CommonHooks   -- everything else
# Deliberately unmapped, no replacement exists:
#   AttachCapabilitiesEvent (86)  capabilities are no longer attached to objects
#   FillBucketEvent (6)           replaced by fluid capability interactions
#   LootingLevelEvent (7)         removed by the 1.21 enchantment rework
# METHOD_TO_STATIC  owner <TAB> name <TAB> desc <TAB> newOwner <TAB> newName <TAB> newDesc
# For the case neither a rename nor a shim can reach: a type that MUST be renamed, because the
# loader dispatches on it and a shimmed copy would never fire, whose replacement is missing a
# method the corpus calls. RegisterEvent is the first instance -- placebo calls
# getForgeRegistry() on it, and NeoForge dropped that method.
# The rewrite is cheap because the stack already suits it: when INVOKEVIRTUAL runs, the receiver
# sits below the arguments in exactly the slot INVOKESTATIC reads its first parameter from. So
# the owner becomes the first descriptor argument and nothing has to be shuffled.
# Owners here are written POST-rename -- these rules run after the type remapper, so the owner
# is already net/neoforged/... even though the mod was compiled against net/minecraftforge/...
# This is the shape for the rest of the "rename target missing a called member" list in
# api-report/unresolved-types.txt, which currently runs to several hundred entries.
METHOD_TO_STATIC
# common/util was a prefix rule and should not have been.
# The package is split down the middle. NeoForge kept FakePlayer, Lazy, ITeleporter and friends
# at the same path, so those rename cleanly. It also kept INBTSerializable there -- with
# different method signatures. Its serializeNBT/deserializeNBT gained a HolderLookup.Provider
# parameter in 1.20.5, when NBT started needing registry access, so a Forge implementor
# overrides nothing and leaves the real interface methods abstract. 61 jars implement it.
# LazyOptional and the NonNull* functional interfaces have no NeoForge equivalent at all and are
# shimmed; the prefix rule was harmless for them only because the target-existence check refused
# it. Relying on that is relying on an accident.
# So: enumerate the ones that genuinely moved, and let everything else fall through to a shim.
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
# FIELD_RETYPE  owner <TAB> newFieldDescriptor
# 1.21 turned several holder classes from enums implementing the thing they described into plain
# carriers of Holder<T> constants. ArmorMaterials.IRON went from an ArmorMaterials enum constant
# implementing ArmorMaterial to a Holder<ArmorMaterial>, and ArmorItem's constructor changed to
# match.
# The field names did not change, so neither the SRG mapping nor any type rename touches this.
# Only the descriptor moved -- and the verifier reads descriptors, so this fails before the code
# runs, as a VerifyError rather than a NoSuchFieldError. geckolib and aquaculture both die here.
# Per-owner rather than per-field: the wrapping was wholesale, so enumerating the constants would
# be one chance per constant to miss one, and a missed one fails identically.
FIELD_RETYPE
# The consuming constructor. Argument order is unchanged, so this is a plain call-site rewrite
# and RENAME_METHOD covers it -- INVOKESPECIAL is preserved and only the descriptor moves.
RENAME_METHOD
# ItemHandlerHelper kept most of its class in NeoForge but lost these two, both of which
# vanilla absorbed in 1.20.5 when component comparison replaced NBT comparison. Static to
# static, so a plain call-site rewrite covers them. Owners are post-rename. 47 and 39 jars.
RENAME_METHOD
RENAME_METHOD
# IEventBus.post returned boolean in Forge and returns the event in NeoForge. The shim extends
# NeoForge s interface, so declaring both is a clashing-erasure compile error -- no shim and no
# rename can express a return-type change on an inherited method. The call site moves instead.
# 110 jars. Owner is the Forge name because IEventBus is shimmed, not renamed.
METHOD_TO_STATIC
# ModConfigEvent is renamed (the mod bus dispatches on it), so its getConfig() returns NeoForge s
# ModConfig where the mod expects Forge s. The class resolves and the call does not. The subclass
# entries are separate because the owner in the bytecode is whichever type the listener declared.
METHOD_TO_STATIC
METHOD_TO_STATIC
METHOD_TO_STATIC
